title: Metropolis Random Walks Escape Deep Basins Faster in Higher Dimensions

folio.blurb: How long does a random walk take to escape a deep cubic basin? Matching bounds show how dimension changes the mean escape time. The proof compares an electrical network with a chain of shells, then constructs a flow through the basin.

figure.alt: Square terraces around the origin show the nested shells of a two-dimensional cubic basin of depth four.
figure.caption: Fig. 1 · The two-dimensional cubic basin

paper_overview: The paper studies how dimension changes the time a Metropolis random walk takes to escape a deep cubic basin. It compares the full walk with a chain that averages over shells and proves matching asymptotic escape-time bounds.

lem:transport.summary: For every positive dimension and every radius, the proof constructs currents on nearest-neighbor cube edges. At each vertex their divergence is the difference of the two uniform densities. Their total squared energy is at most n/(k+1)^n. The tuple coordinates translate the integer cube and enumerate each positive-direction edge once.

lem:hitting.summary: Expected hitting time from a point is related to its capacity and a weighted sum of hitting probabilities.
lem:hitting.step: Lean checked detailed balance for the killed occupation kernel. The first-entrance decomposition and its connection to Dirichlet capacity are in progress.
lem:hitting.next: Identify the first-entrance and capacity factors for the lattice walk.

thm:asymptotic.summary: For each integer dimension at least one and fixed 0 < p < 1, the expected escape time is the tail sum of the killed shell chain starting at zero. The proof uses its exact finite-sum formula and bounds a polynomially weighted geometric series to obtain the two-sided Big Theta asymptotic in the paper.

thm:exact-escape.summary: For each positive dimension, depth and 0 < p ≤ 1, the survival probabilities of the shell-averaged walk are summable. Their sum equals the manuscript’s displayed formula. In dimension one, the signed Metropolis walk has the same expected escape time.
